tower.plan.title: Plan versus actual
tower.plan.hint: Every parcel taken in at a counter is given a route and a time it should be ready to collect, and both are kept. This holds each lane against that promise — the last 30 days, the lanes most often late first. A lane habitually late, or not going the way it was planned, shows here and nowhere else.

tower.corridors.title: Corridors
tower.corridors.lede: The bus routes this network runs, between one zone and another. The network draws its own here; a fleet may propose a line it runs itself, and nothing routes on that line until it is published here. A shop reads them without knowing they exist.
tower.corridors.caveatT: A corridor decides what a shop may take in.
tower.corridors.caveat: A parcel crossing zones can only be accepted where a corridor serves that pair and no hub can carry it instead. Closing one stops those take-ins straight away; shifts already running on it keep running, and the buses still finish today.
tower.corridors.emptyBody: Until one is drawn, no shop can take in a parcel bound for another zone unless a hub can route it.
tower.corridors.col.name: Corridor
tower.corridors.f.name: Name
tower.corridors.needZones: A corridor runs from one zone to another — name both ends.
tower.corridors.sameZone: Both ends are the same zone. A corridor is only ever consulted for a parcel crossing zones, so this one would never be used.
tower.corridors.duplicate: There is already an open corridor for that pair, and only the first would ever be found. Close that one first, or draw the return leg.
tower.corridors.drawn: Corridor drawn — shops in that zone can take parcels for it now.
tower.corridors.closed: Corridor closed — no shop can take in new parcels for that pair.
tower.corridors.published: Line published — shops in that zone can take parcels for it now, and only that fleet’s drivers run it.

tower.money.title: Money
tower.money.lede: What this company holds, what it owes, and paying the people it owes it to.
tower.money.tax.title: Tax invoices (KRA eTIMS)
tower.biz.fact.systemNone: No address given: nothing is sent
tower.money.tax.rail.kra: Every sale and every sale given back is numbered in one series and recorded with KRA.
tower.money.tax.rail.kraTest: Recorded with KRA’s test system, not with KRA itself: nothing here counts for tax yet.
tower.money.tax.rail.stand_in: A stand-in answers on this laptop: nothing goes to KRA, and every invoice says SANDBOX.
tower.money.tax.rail.not_set_up: eTIMS is not set up on this server: invoices are made, numbered and wait. Nothing is sent to KRA.
tower.money.tax.heldBehind: The invoices after it wait until it is sent again.
tower.money.caveatLead: Nothing on this screen moves money.
tower.money.caveat: A run RAISES payouts, a second member of staff approves each one to its rail, and only the rail’s answer changes what the books say. By M-Pesa that answer arrives by itself; by hand it is somebody pressing a button with the reference — so this console never becomes a place where money is declared paid because a screen said so.
tower.money.waitsForMpesa: M-Pesa answers this one: its result marks it paid or failed.
tower.money.morning.ran: The system raises this run every morning at {at}, on the company’s own clock — last on {day} — and emails the staff who hold the money role when it has payouts in it. One of them checks it and approves sending.
tower.money.morning.notYet: The system raises this run every morning at {at}, on the company’s own clock — it has not run yet — and emails the staff who hold the money role when it has payouts in it. One of them checks it and approves sending.
tower.money.emptyBody: And nobody is waiting: no payout has been raised for this company. Running one raises what today’s work owes, and skips anybody the cover cannot carry — it says who, and why.
tower.money.how.byHand: By hand: paid outside SeeBuyGet, the reference recorded here
tower.money.receipt: M-Pesa receipt, from the M-Pesa portal
tower.money.runRaised: Raised {n, plural, one {# payout} other {# payouts}} for {day}.
tower.money.runRaisedNone: Nothing to raise for {day} — nobody is owed anything today.
tower.money.in.title: Money coming in
tower.money.in.lede: A shop asking to top up moves nothing. The balance — and the cash figure above — change when a payment provider confirms the payment, at the amount the provider confirms.
tower.money.in.emptyTitle: Nobody has asked to pay anything in
tower.money.in.emptyBody: When a shop or a store asks to top up, it appears here with the reference they were told to quote, and waits until a payment is confirmed against it.
tower.money.in.refTitle: What is the payment’s own reference?
tower.money.in.refBody: The statement line, the M-Pesa code, the transfer reference — something somebody can look up afterwards. This is what makes it a confirmed payment rather than a claim.
tower.money.in.sandboxNote: Sandbox only: this signs a callback exactly as the payment provider would and sends it through the same door, signature check included.
tower.money.in.unmatchedTitle: Money we cannot put a name to
tower.money.in.unmatchedLede: Payments that arrived quoting no reference, or one nobody is waiting on. They are recorded and deliberately NOT posted: we do not know whose book they belong in, and a guess in the books is worse than a hole in them. That is also why they are listed whichever company is selected — they belong to none of them yet.
tower.money.in.unmatchedCol.why: Why it could not be matched
tower.money.in.applyBody: Reference {ref}. It could not be matched because {reason}.
tower.money.in.applyCaveat: This credits the money to whoever you pick, and it can only be done once — the payment arrived once. Your name is recorded against it.
tower.money.in.applySuggest: Waiting for a payment like this
tower.money.in.applySearch: Search shops by name or zone
tower.money.in.held.title: Paybill payments M-Pesa has not confirmed
tower.money.in.held.lede: M-Pesa’s notice of a paybill payment proves only where it came from, so we ask M-Pesa about each one before it is credited. These it has not confirmed. Look for each on the M-Pesa statement: credit it if it is there, refuse it if it is not.
